**Current behavior**
<!-- Describe how the bug manifests. -->
Compiling using `ngc` and with `flatModuleOutFile` produces a `*.metadata.json` file with flattened html/css paths.

Example:
```
// ...
"arguments": [
  {
    "selector": "my-lib",
    "templateUrl": "./lib.component.html",
    "styleUrls": [
      "./lib.component.css"
    ]
  }
]
// ...
```
**Expected behavior**
<!-- Describe what the behavior would be without the bug. -->
Paths to html/css should be resolved to the original path. Notice `./lib/...`:
```
// ...
"arguments": [
  {
    "selector": "my-lib",
    "templateUrl": "./lib/lib.component.html",
    "styleUrls": [
      "./lib/lib.component.css"
    ]
  }
]
// ...
```

**Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions**
<!--
If the current behavior is a bug or you can illustrate your feature request better with an example, 
please provide the *STEPS TO REPRODUCE* and if possible a *MINIMAL DEMO* of the problem via
https://plnkr.co or similar (you can use this template as a starting point: http://plnkr.co/edit/tpl:AvJOMERrnz94ekVua0u5).
-->
```
git clone https://github.com/filipesilva/ngc-flatmodule-windows
cd ngc-flatmodule-windows
npm run build
```

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**
<!-- Describe the motivation or the concrete use case -->
Library authors should not have to copy all html/css to the root `typings/` folder instead of maintaining the library structure.

Flattening the html/css paths to root also forces library authors to avoid duplicate html/css filenames.
